body.name: deterministic Algorithms 1--2 task machine
body.construction:
Define \(\operatorname{next}_I\) by exhaustive case analysis on the canonically least current work task and the result.  It implements Algorithm 1 lines 1--18 and Algorithm 2 lines 1--9 exactly as specified in the four transition definitions.  It computes every closure, district, context graph, d-separation test, valid fixing sequence, truncated factor, hybrid kernel, and continuation from \(I\) and the current state fields.  A failed LGS line creates the correspondingly tagged residual task; an invariant failure after a computed valid sequence is an internal rejection of the purported state, not a semantic branch.  Candidate exhaustion yields \(\operatorname{ResidualPending}\).

For a task \(\tau\), let
\[
 r_I(\tau)=
 (|\operatorname{random\ ambient}(\tau)|,
   c(\tau),f(\tau),k(\tau))
\]
with lexicographic order, where the finite control levels strictly descend through
\[
 \operatorname{Start}>\operatorname{District\ tests}>
 \operatorname{closure\ fixing}>\operatorname{postclosure}>
 \operatorname{A2\ scan}>\operatorname{hybrid\ fixing}>
 \operatorname{Factor}>\operatorname{Join},
\]
\(f\) is the remaining fixing-sequence length, and \(k\) is the remaining candidate count.  The machine measure \(\mu_H\) is the Dershowitz--Manna finite-multiset extension of this rank over \(\operatorname{Work}\).  The canonical encoding orders productive tasks before a dependent Join and orders every set, sequence, and candidate topologically and then lexicographically.  The machine starts at \(\operatorname{init}_H(I)\) and iterates \(\operatorname{next}_I\) until a formula, a verified twin, or a residual-pending result is returned.
